newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.55 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.55 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt an average 2.55 percent on Tuesday, in continued selective activity after Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the recent rally, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 gained 29 points to close at a new all-time high of 1,165, compared to Friday's previous record of 1,153. In dollar terms, it was unchanged from Friday's record high $1.04, and firmed from Monday's $1.02.
Trade volume leapt to 21.14 trillion lira ($189.1 million) from Monday's 14.48 trillion lira ($129.8 million).
Brokers said selective demand continued from the first session as players switched to cheaper shares from those with stronger premiums, with the help of rising liquidity.

The index which hit a midday record of 1,168 at the end of the first session, had surged 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consequtive days after the market reopened on January 2, following a five-day holiday.
Downward money and bond market rates, quiet trends in the currency market and 1996 profit prospects of companies were the main factors behind the latest uptrend.
